notes: All 4 cases match between Java oracle trace and Go test assertions. constant-insertinto: consumer receives events in precedence order (5,4,3,2,1,0); window iteration order also follows precedence order (5,4,3,2,1,0) — verified by Java oracle only (Go implementation does not support inserting into a named window from a regular select statement). constant-merge-table: insert-into actions execute in precedence order (c,a,b). constant-merge-window: insert-into actions execute in precedence order (c,a,b). constant-on-split: split-stream branches execute in precedence order (3,2,1). Go implementation: (1) regular insert-into routes events with precedence via EventPrecedence option; (2) merge-into table/window routes insert-into actions with precedence via ThenInsertIntoWithPrecedence; (3) split-stream routes branches with precedence via SplitIntoWithPrecedence/SplitIntoWhenWithPrecedence.

4.342 extension (ords 4/9): nonconst-contained-event replays the two-level contained-event routes LvlA[b]->LvlB and LvlB[c]->LvlC, each with event-precedence(precedence) evaluated against the routed target event; chained routes interleave through the shared precedence queue and the flattened LvlC id order per LvlA send matches the Java pins (C,B,D,A / C,A,B,D / A,B,C,D / H,D,A,G,F,B,I,E,C / B,G,H,D,F,A,C,I,E). constant-output-rate replays the three output-every-2-events routes with precedences 1/2/3 and per-statement id offsets 1/2/3 (Java's computeEventPrecedence(3, *) static call over the routed output event is pinned as the constant 3 in Go — approved adaptation); two sends produce one batch ordered 13,23,12,22,11,21 (precedence across statements, FIFO within). The oracle registers mirror classes/computeEventPrecedence locally because the run-script classpath excludes regression-lib; shapes and semantics replicate the suite byte-for-byte.

4.343 extension (ords 5-8, ENGINE unit): the event-precedence expressions now register their subqueries (visitQueryExpressions visits query.eventPrecedence, merge-action and split-branch precedence) and evaluate with the statement's attached variables (route and split paths), and TriggerQuery.Query copies spec.eventPrecedence for on-select routes — previously subquery precedence silently degraded to 0 (FIFO). The four routed contexts replay one contract: a,b with null subqueries, b,a after priming N(1,2), a,b after N(2,1) (insertinto uses N(-2,-1)). The OnDemand query now also copies eventPrecedence, making the FAF rejection live. The oracle gained a multi-module deploy convention and an @FAF module for the ord-8 window pre-population; SupportBeanNumeric is a local mirror class (run-script classpath excludes regression-lib).

4.344 closes the class with ord 10 (EPLInsertIntoEventPrecInvalid) registered implemented-not-DV per the invalidity policy — no trace rows: a Build-time validateEventPrecedence pass now mirrors Java's validateEventPrecedence across route, split-branch and named-window-merge paths (integer-typed expressions only; property references resolve against the output event type only; subquery-internal expressions resolve against their own source). Review follow-up: the table-merge path (table-merge clause actions, distinct from the route path) also validates event-precedence with the same integer rule — Java validates table and named-window merges alike. Approved differences: message texts are engine-internal; the FAF sub-case rejects with the Go message; the table-target precedence rejection exists for the pre-registered-target reason; the reserved-keyword parse error is unrepresentable in the typed API. Class disposition 10/11 DV + 1 implemented-not-DV.
